record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: What smoothness properties can hyperboloidal initial data have at a possibly generalized conformal infinity, and what are the weakest such conditions under which positivity of the Bondi mass can be proved?

evidence.quote: Classify the various kinds of smoothness properties which hyperboloidal initial data may have at (a possibly generalised) conformal infinity. In particular, find the weakest conditions under which a proof of positivity of the Bondi mass can be completed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g,K)$ be a 3-dimensional asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations (or for the Einstein equations with non-negative matter satisfying the dominant energy condition), meaning that $(M,g)$ admits a conformal compactification: there exists a manifold-with-boundary $\widetilde M = M \cup \mathscr{I}$ and a defining function $\Omega \geq 0$ for $\mathscr{I} = \partial \widetilde M$ such that $\tilde g = \Omega^2 g$ extends to $\widetilde M$, with $K$ satisfying suitable asymptotic conditions making $\mathscr{I}$ play the role of (a piece of) future null infinity. The Trautman–Bondi mass is defined as a flux/boundary integral at $\mathscr{I}$ in terms of the conformal data.
 
Possible regularity hypotheses at $\mathscr{I}$ include: $C^\infty$ compactifications, $C^k$ compactifications for finite $k$, polyhomogeneous compactifications (asymptotic expansions in powers of $\Omega$ and $\log\Omega$), and more general weighted Sobolev or Hölder asymptotics. One may also allow a generalized conformal infinity (e.g., of non-spherical topology or with degeneracies of the conformal factor).
 
(a) Classify the possible smoothness and asymptotic-regularity classes (smooth, finite differentiability, polyhomogeneous, with prescribed leading log terms, etc.) that hyperboloidal initial data sets may exhibit at a possibly generalized conformal infinity, in a manner compatible with the constraint equations.
 
(b) Determine the weakest such regularity/asymptotic conditions at $\mathscr{I}$ under which the Trautman–Bondi mass is well-defined and a proof of its positivity (under the dominant energy condition, with equality only in Minkowski space) can be carried through.
artifact.status_search_result: Positivity of the Trautman–Bondi mass has been established under several regularity classes, notably by Chruściel, Jezierski, and Łęski for spherical conformal infinity with polyhomogeneous compactifications, and extended to higher dimensions. Recent work (2025) on hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities further refines the smoothness picture. However, a complete classification of all admissible smoothness/asymptotic classes at a generalized conformal infinity and identification of the truly weakest conditions for the positivity proof has not been fully achieved, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The Trautman-Bondi mass of hyperboloidal initial data sets
status_evidence.snippet: Definition of mass for conformally compactifiable initial data sets, proving positivity of this Trautman-Bondi mass in the case of spherical conformal infinity; polyhomogeneous compactifications allowed.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity proved under polyhomogeneous compactifications with spherical conformal infinity.

status_evidence.title: Bondi Mass Cannot Become Negative in Higher Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Extension of Bondi-mass positivity to higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Positivity results extended beyond the original setting.

status_evidence.title: Hyperboloidal initial data without logarithmic singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of well-defined Bondi mass together with mild restrictions implies generic solutions of the parabolic-hyperbolic constraints are free of logarithmic singularities.
status_evidence.claim: Recent refinements link Bondi mass to smoothness/polyhomogeneity, but a full classification remains incomplete.
